transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, honestly, I'm here because I just... I can't sleep anymore. And it's not like I'm not tired. I am so, so exhausted by the end of the day. I mean, my job—I'm a sales manager, and it's just non-stop. So by the time I get home, make dinner, try to unwind, I feel like I could sleep for a week. But then I get into bed, and it's like my brain just decides it's time to work the night shift. I just lie there, staring at the ceiling, and every single sales forecast, every little issue with my team, every email I didn't get to, it all just starts playing on a loop in my head. I try everything, you know? Deep breathing, reading, making lists so I don't forget things, but it doesn't matter. And then, if I do finally manage to drift off, I always—without fail—wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. And that's it. The sleep is over. I just lie there in the dark, and my brain is completely wired again, going over the exact same things, just spinning and spinning. It's gotten so unreliable, and I'm just running on fumes at this point, and I really don't know how much longer I can keep doing this because it's affecting everything...
Do you find that you worry excessively about things, even when you try not to, or feel like your anxiety is difficult to control?

Oh, completely. It's... it's like I have absolutely no control over the steering wheel in my own head. I mean, I really do try to stop it. I sit there and I literally talk to myself, sometimes even out loud if I'm alone. I'll say, 'Brenda, you've done the plan, you've looked at the numbers, just let it go.' And for a second, maybe a minute or two, I think I've actually reasoned with myself and I can finally relax. 

But then, I swear, not even five minutes later, I am right back in another loop. It's just so incredibly frustrating because I'll figure one thing out, right? I'll mentally check one concern off my list—like, okay, the quarterly projections are handled, I sent the email, that's done. But the second I check that one thing off, it's like three more completely new worries just pop right up to take its place. 

And then suddenly I'm worrying about whether the client is going to push back on the pricing, or if my boss thinks I'm not pushing the sales team hard enough this month, or if I forgot to CC someone important on that email I just sent... and it just snowballs. I try to put a lid on it, I really do, because I know logically that it's not productive to just sit there agonizing over things I can't even fix right that second, but it just doesn't matter. The thoughts just keep coming and coming, and they just bounce around in there no matter how hard I try to just shut them down and force myself to stop caring for five minutes.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. Not at all, really. I mean, I'm incredibly frustrated, obviously, but I don't feel sad or down in the dumps. And as for losing interest... no, I still want to do all the things I usually love. 

Like, I'm a huge baker. I love spending my weekends trying out new pastry recipes, and I still get really excited when I see a new recipe online or in a magazine. I'll bookmark it, I'll even go to the grocery store and buy all the specific ingredients—like the expensive vanilla or whatever it calls for. But then Sunday comes, and I'm just so completely drained from the lack of sleep, and my mind is already racing so fast about the Monday morning pipeline review, that I just can't bring myself to actually stand in the kitchen for three hours. But it's not because I don't care anymore! I still really, really want to do it. It's just that the worry kind of eats up all the space and energy I have for it. 

It's the exact same thing with seeing my friends. They'll text the group chat and want to get dinner or grab drinks, and I really want to go and catch up with everyone, I really do. But then I just start thinking about how exhausted I'll be the next day, and how I still need to prep for work, and I just end up staying home. So the interest is one hundred percent still there, it's just... I'm too tired and wound up to actually participate in my own life right now, if that makes sense. But no, definitely not hopeless or depressed. Just running on empty.
Do you ever feel physically restless, tense, or fatigued during the day as a result of not sleeping well or worrying so much?

Oh, God, yes. The physical part is almost as bad as the mental part. I am just... I feel wound up almost all the time. It's this constant, buzzing, nervous energy, but not a good, productive energy, you know? It's like my body is constantly bracing for an impact that never actually comes. 

I could be doing the most completely mundane thing—like, I'll just be sitting at my kitchen island, eating dinner, maybe having some pasta I managed to throw together, and my stomach is tight and my body is on edge exactly like I'm sitting right in the middle of a high-stakes pipeline review with the regional director. Like, why does my body think eating a bowl of penne in my own house is a high-pressure sales pitch? It makes no sense! 

And my muscles... especially my neck and my shoulders. They are just rock hard all day. I'll catch myself hiking my shoulders all the way up to my ears while I'm typing emails, and I'll consciously tell myself, 'Brenda, drop your shoulders, take a deep breath.' And I'll lower them, I'll physically force them down. But I swear, two seconds later, I'm thinking about a client call and they are right back up there, tight as a drum. I've tried taking boiling hot showers, I even bought one of those expensive massage guns online last month because I thought maybe I could just physically pummel the knots out while I watch TV, but my shoulders stay tight no matter how much I try to relax. It's like the tension is just permanently baked into my muscles at this point. 

And the fatigue... well, hauling around all this tight muscle and nervous energy all day, on top of the awful sleep... it just drains every single drop of energy I have. By two in the afternoon, I'll literally just be sitting at my desk and my whole body feels like it's vibrating because I'm so incredibly exhausted and yet completely wired at the exact same time. It's just exhausting to be in my own body right now.
